prompt: The amount of medicine in the blood is $C(t) = \frac{20t}{t^2 + 4}$ milligrams per liter after $t$ hours. What is $C(2)$?
hint: Substitute $t = 2$ into the top AND the bottom separately.

hints.text: Substitute $t = 2$ into the top AND the bottom separately.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\frac{10t}{t^2 + 1}$ at $t = 3$: top is 30, bottom is $9 + 1 = 10$, so the answer is 3. Same three steps here.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the medicine fade
steps: At $t = 6$: $\frac{120}{40} = 3$ mg/L, fading. The bottom eventually grows faster, so the level slides back toward 0.
